value.title: Procedures in a template (workstream 010 s01)
value.summary: A pod template carries procedures about the pod itself and links procedures in the repo; its procedures and seed text carry what pij does not do, such as creating a run's branch and worktree or asking seats in training not to read earlier runs.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: A pod template carries procedures about the pod itself and links procedures in the repo; its procedures and seed text carry what pij does not do, such as creating a run's branch and worktree or asking seats in training not to read earlier runs.

sections.name: goals
value: A template brings how to run it, and what pij leaves to it, wherever it goes.

value.claim: A template folder may hold `procedures/<PROC-id>/` (PRD 005's layout) and a list of linked repo procedures; `pij proc` runs both by id from a pod's template path.
Adopting a template into another repo brings its own procedures and reports each linked one missing there.
The docs and an example template show a branch-and-worktree procedure and a training-mode seed line; `pod up` creates neither and pij walls nothing off.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Procedures: skills/pij/procedures and harness/scripts/procedures (PRD 005); pod templates (plan 247).

value.risk: A template's procedure collides with a repo procedure id.
value.mitigation: Ids are scoped by the template's path; the run names which it used.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: on demand only: reading a template's procedures is in-process. No loop, poll or timer.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
